answer: Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The marble lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the plume is where a second reviewer recomputes them. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the falcon of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work.
